Degree-preserving edge-swap null for co-expressolog statistics

Source: R/coexpressolog_null.R
coexpressolog_null.Rd

Tests whether an observed co-expressolog statistic exceeds what network topology alone produces. Each species network is binarised at its analysis threshold and rewired by degree-preserving edge swaps, which keep every gene's degree but destroy the correspondence between network neighbourhoods and the ortholog mapping. find_coexpressologs then runs on the rewired networks with exactly the same arguments (...) as the observed run, and the statistic is compared against the resulting null distribution.

coexpressolog_null(
  networks,
  orthologs,
  statistic = NULL,
  n_perm = 100L,
  swap_factor = 10L,
  n_cores = 1L,
  seed = NULL,
  filter_zero = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

networks

Named list of sparse network objects (compute_network(sparse = TRUE) outputs), keyed by species abbreviation. Dense networks are rejected; convert them with as_sparse_network.

orthologs

Data frame with columns Species1, Species2, hog, as for find_coexpressologs.

statistic

Function mapping the find_coexpressologs() edge data frame to a named numeric vector, or NULL (default) for the count of rows with type == "conserved" per species pair (named paste(species1, species2, sep = "~")) plus "total". For the built-in statistic, a null run whose rewiring leaves a species pair with no overlap > 0 rows records 0 conserved calls for that pair; a user-supplied statistic missing a name from the observed run errors.

n_perm

Number of rewired permutations (default 100).

swap_factor

Swap trials per permutation, rejected ones included, as a multiple of the edge count of each thresholded network (default 10). Must be a single finite number > 0. The trial count is rounded up, so any positive factor makes at least one trial on a network with two or more edges; a network with fewer than two edges has no swap to make and is returned unchanged.

n_cores

Number of parallel workers for the permutation loop (default 1).

seed

Base seed for the run. NULL (default) draws one from the ambient RNG stream and leaves it advanced by that one draw, so consecutive unseeded calls give different nulls and a set.seed() in the caller's script reproduces the whole run. With a seed the call draws from a private stream and restores the caller's on exit — the package-wide contract, see detect_modules.

What a default call guarantees is replayability, not a fixed null. The seed actually used — drawn or supplied — is recorded as attr(result, "seed"), and a drawn one is also announced in a message, so any run can be reproduced exactly by passing that value back as seed. Two default calls return different nulls; the size of that difference is what null_se and the p_emp_lo / p_emp_hi interval report. The default was 1L before 0.3.0, which pinned the null of every default call while leaving the observed statistic free to drift, and hid the Monte Carlo error entirely.

Two seeds exactly 2^31 - 1 apart (both legal, since a seed may lie anywhere in +/- .Machine$integer.max) give every rewiring permutation the same seed, so the null is identical for the two runs even though the observed statistic is not: see the aliasing note under .task_seed().

filter_zero

Passed to find_coexpressologs for both the observed and every null run. TRUE (default) drops ortholog pairs with zero neighbourhood overlap before the q-values, which is what this test wants: the statistic reads called edges only, so retaining the zero-overlap rows adds tens of thousands of never-called rows per pair to every permutation for nothing. It also differs from the find_coexpressologs() default, which keeps them so that low-degree failures carry a power value.

...

Passed unchanged to find_coexpressologs for both the observed and every null run (species_pairs, method, alternative, alpha, pval_combine, pi0_method, ...).

Value

Data frame with one row per statistic and columns statistic, observed, null_mean, null_sd, null_max, fold (observed / null_mean; NA when the null mean is 0), p_emp ((1 + n_ge) / (n_perm + 1)), n_ge (null draws at or above the observed value), null_se (null_sd / sqrt(n_perm), the Monte Carlo error of null_mean; the relative error of fold is null_se / null_mean, which is large whenever null_mean is near 0) and p_emp_lo / p_emp_hi, an exact Clopper-Pearson 95\ probability that p_emp estimates — an interval on that probability, not on p_emp itself. The n_perm x k matrix of null statistics is attached as attr(, "null"), and the base seed the run used as attr(, "seed").

Details

Rewiring operates on the network thresholded at net$threshold (the analysis density), not on the stored superset: sparse-store entries with values at or above the threshold become edges, the rest are dropped. The rewired networks are unweighted (every stored value is 1, with threshold = 1 and store_threshold = 1), so only membership-based consumers are valid downstream; edge weights carry no information after rewiring. A network with m edges gets ceiling(swap_factor * m) swap trials, each the trial of igraph's keeping_degseq() rewiring: two distinct edges are drawn uniformly, a swap that would create a loop or a multi-edge is rejected, and the rejected trial still counts. Counting it is what makes the chain sample the realizations of a degree sequence uniformly. Networks stay simple (no loops, no multi-edges). Adjacency is held as an n x n bit matrix during rewiring, n^2 / 8 bytes per network per worker (32 MB at 16 000 genes).

Permutation b runs in a worker that seeds itself from the base seed and its own index (the package-wide per-task seed derivation), so results are reproducible, independent of n_cores, and two neighbouring base seeds share no rewiring. On Unix the permutations run under parallel::mclapply(); on Windows they run serially. The seed covers the observed run as well as the null runs, so ... settings that draw — the default pi0_method = "randomized", for one — are pinned too. method = "permutation" in ... is allowed but slow (a full permutation test per rewired network).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- coexpressolog_null(networks, orthologs,
  n_perm = 100L,
  n_cores = 4L
)
res[res$statistic == "total", ]

# replay that exact run, whether or not it was seeded
same <- coexpressolog_null(networks, orthologs,
  n_perm = 100L,
  n_cores = 4L, seed = attr(res, "seed")
)
} # }
